question: How many US circuit court judges will be confirmed during November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Exactly two circuit nominees are pending on the Senate floor: Domenico (10th Cir., reported 7/23) and St. John (5th Cir., reported 9/24); both were left pending when the Senate adjourned until Nov 9. Rudofsky (8th Cir.) had his hearing ~Sept 30, and per the Balls & Strikes timeline cannot reach the floor before ~Dec 7, so 3+ needs an unusual acceleration. November has ~8 session days (Nov 9-10, the week of Nov 16, Nov 30; out Nov 11-13 and the week of Nov 23). December has 14 days, so one or both votes could slip there, and lame-duck priorities or attendance could crowd judges out; the GOP's steady focus on confirming judges argues for votes soon after return. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Two circuit nominees are waiting for a floor vote: Domenico (10th Cir., on the calendar since 7/23) and St. John (5th Cir., since 9/24). Rudofsky (8th Cir.) only had his hearing on 9/30. Butler (5th Cir.) was nominated 10/1 and has had no hearing. The Senate adjourned on 10/1 and returns the week of Nov 9, with only about 8 session days scheduled in November. Republicans are under lame-duck pressure to confirm judges, and in Nov 2025 the Senate confirmed two circuit judges in one week. So confirming both calendared nominees in November is the most likely single outcome. Pulling the other way: Domenico sat on the calendar through all of September without a vote; each circuit nominee can take up to 30 hours of post-cloture floor time; and government funding (deadline Dec 11) plus the 14 December session days could push the votes into December. That is especially likely if Republicans keep the Senate and feel less urgency. Rudofsky reaching the floor in November would need committee action fast enough to beat Balls & Strikes' estimate of a Dec 7 floor date. No human market found: the harness found nothing on Polymarket or Manifold, and my search turned up no Kalshi or bookmaker contract.

calls.reasoning: Only Domenico (10th Cir.) and St. John (5th Cir.) are floor-ready; Rudofsky can't plausibly reach the floor before ~Dec 7. The Senate returns Nov 9, but its first vote is a legislative cloture vote (H.R.2347), and the lame duck effectively starts Nov 16, breaks for Thanksgiving, and resumes Nov 30. That leaves roughly one full week plus a few days for judges in November. Paired circuit confirmations in a single week are common (Nov 2025), and Thune has named judges a priority. But Domenico went unconfirmed through September, funding (deadline Dec 11), the farm bill and the defense bill compete for floor time, and December has 14 session days for slippage. Net: 2 is the modal outcome, with 0 or 1 jointly more likely. No human market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) how much November floor time exists; (2) whether cloture was already filed; (3) a snippet claiming Domenico was confirmed 57-42; (4) how much priority judges get. Checks: the Senate Democrats' floor schedule and news reports show the Senate returning Nov 9 with a single 5:30pm cloture vote on H.R.2347, a legislative bill, not a judge. Bloomberg/Balls & Strikes describe the lame duck commencing Nov 16, breaking Thanksgiving week and returning Nov 30, so the November window is narrower than '8 days' implied. A search for Domenico cloture found no filing; nominationnotes still lists both as pending; no confirmation. The 57-42 snippet is unsupported. Judgment on floor priority is unresolved; the narrower window and Domenico's long idle period push weight toward 0, ending near Runs 2-3 rather than Run 1.
